newsitem.title: USA: N.J. school plan may raise taxes 7 pct -- paper.
newsitem.headline: N.J. school plan may raise taxes 7 pct -- paper.

text.p: A new study found that a proposed school finance reform plan in New Jersey could force increases in local school taxes an average of 7.4 percent, the Star Ledger reported Wednesday.
The report, from the state's Office of Legislative Services, said Newark could see the highest increase, at 73 percent.

The proposed reforms are at the center of an ongoing legislative debate in New Jersey, which is under a court-imposed deadline of Dec 31 to find a way to equalize spending between rich and poor school districts.
The Legislature's plan calls for an overall increase of 6.8 percent in state aid to schools.

Gov Christine Whitman has proposed a slightly different reform plan than the one now under consideration in the Legislature. An administration official said the OLS study used unrealistic assumptions.
